18:11076-1984 

Indian Standard 

GUIDE FOR PALLETIZATION OF 
CASHEW KERNELS FOR EXPORT 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 31 August 1984, after the draft finalized by Pallets Sectional Com- 
mittee had been approved by Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging 
Division Council. 

0.2 A bulk of the cashew kernel produce of our country is exported. In 
export, unitization of loads has assumed a very important place in view of 
the mechanization of handling of cargo at the various points. In trans- 
portation, imitization has been found to be an extremely useful operation 
for economizing in handling in terms of both time and reduced damages. 
The form of unitization is by both palletization and by containerization of 
pallets. 

0.3 As per existing practice, cashew kernels are packed in 18-litre square 
tins and this standard has been proposed with this as the basis. 

0.4 It is essential that guidelines are drawn up to facilitate the preparation 
of export cargo by the exporters who appreciate the problem and would 
like to take advantage of the modern trend in unitization. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard lays down the guidelines for palletization of cashew 
kernels for export and for containerization of the palletized loads. 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the terms and definitions as given in 
IS : 3971-1976* and IS : 65694972t shall apply. 

3. PACKAGES 

3.1 Two tins of cashew kernels shall be placed in a fibreboard box con- 
forming to IS : 2771 (Part 1)-1977J with plan dimension ( 400 mm x 
600 mm ) as shown in Fig. 1. The height of the box shall be 260 mm.

3.1.1 This size, which conforms to IS : 8470-1977*, complies with the 
module of the intermodal transportation system, 

4. PALLETS 

4.1 Single deck board pallets with 4-way free entry expendable pallets 
conforming to IS : 9340-19791 are recommended for the palletization of 
cashew kernels. 

4.2 The following over all plan dimensions of the pallets are considered 

suitable : 

a) 1 200 mm X 1 000 mm.; and 

b) 1 200 mm X 1 800 mm. 

4.3 The general arrangement of packages on the pallets shall be as shown 
in Fig. 2. 

4.4 The number of packages that can be arranged on a pallet shall be as 
under so that the mass and height of the palletized load does not exceed 
1 t and 2 150 mm respectively. 

Size of Pallet Maximum Number of Boxes

General Arrangement of Packages on Pallet 



4,5 Since the pallet is of expendable type, the same may be made from any 
of the species of timber as given in Appendix A of IS : 399-1963* with 
strength coefficient of 75 or more. Species of timber shall be selected to 
meet the desired rated load and application. The selection may also 
depend upon the availability for a particular zone. 

'Classification of commercial timber and their zonal distribution ( rtvistd ).

4.6 The general recommendation for handling of timber pallets as given 
in IS : 8006-1976* shall be taken care of while considering their suitability 
in handling. 

5. FREIGHT CONTAINERS 

5.1 General cargo freight containers conforming to IS : 6929 (Part 1)- 
1973t arc recommended for containerizing the pallets of cashew kernels. 

5.2 Pallets of 1 200 mm x 1 000 mm size are considered suitable for con- 
tainerization : 

5.3 The following dimensions of the containers are considered suitable for 
containerization of pallets :

6. STRAPPING 

6.1 Non-metallic strap shall be used. The strap shall be fastened as tightly 
as possible without damaging the boxes.
